title: How Kubernetes Works in 60 Seconds ☸️ #shorts
description:
Docker runs a container. Kubernetes runs hundreds. A cluster of nodes is managed by a control plane; your containers run in pods; you declare the desired state in YAML; Kubernetes self-heals crashed pods and failed nodes, scales up and down with traffic, and a Service gives your pods one stable address.

#Kubernetes #K8s #DevOps #Docker #CloudComputing #TechExplained #shorts

lines: Docker runs a container. But what happens when you need hundreds?
Kubernetes manages a cluster: a group of machines called nodes, all directed by the control plane, the brain.
Your containers run inside pods, the smallest unit Kubernetes manages. Each pod is scheduled onto a node with room to spare.
You tell Kubernetes what you want, like three copies of my app, in a simple YAML file.
If a pod crashes, or a whole node dies, Kubernetes notices, and starts a replacement automatically.
Traffic spike? It scales from three pods to ten, and back down when things calm down.
And a service gives your pods one stable address, spreading traffic across all of them.
You declare it. Kubernetes keeps it that way.
